newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends lower on China talk, supplies.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends lower on China talk, supplies.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures closed lower on commercial selling which led to talk China may have cancelled orders for U.S. soymeal, traders said.
Continental Grain sold soymeal Monday and Cargill was a key seller Tuesday along with Prudential Securities, traders said.

There were some traders who considered the declines in soymeal a function of a sag in the spot soymeal basis in the United States plus indications of a growing supply of soymeal for export and domestic use.
The soy crush pace has been at historically high levels.
"There were rumors China cancelled meal but they were not confirmed," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Cermak was one of the traders citing the domestic picture as potentially central to the sag in soymeal.
"The large crush numbers have caught up to demand and maybe we're even building some inventory," he said.
Soyoil closed lower on the drop in soybeans, the traders said.
Soymeal closed $0.40 to $2.30 per ton lower, with December down $2.30 at $228.00. Soyoil was 0.05 to 0.18 cent per lb lower, with December down 0.18 at 22.95.
In soymeal, Cargill Inc sold 700 lots of January and Prudential Securities sold 1,000 lots of March, traders said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, below the 18,999 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, above the 18,989 traded Monday.
